abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) remains a challenging malignancy with limited therapeutic options upon relapse/refractory disease, necessitating novel combination strategies. Malignant plasma cells sustain continuous immunoglobulin production, a biosynthetic and secretory burden that places heavy demand on central carbon metabolism and creates potentially targetable metabolic vulnerabilities. Previously, we found a role for HDAC6 in modulating glycolytic metabolism. Our goal here was to find induced metabolic vulnerabilities that could be targeted after HDAC6 inhibition or knockdown. Genetic silencing of HDAC6 or pharmacological inhibition with the selective inhibitor BAS-2, suppressed glycolytic flux, reduced pyruvate and lactate labelling from 13C6-glucose, and remodeled mitochondrial morphology in MM cell lines. Global proteomic analysis revealed coordinated upregulation of amino acid transporters (SLC3A2, SLC7A1, SLC1A5, SLC7A5), and spent-medium measurements confirmed an increased depletion of extracellular amino acids. Collectively, this data indicates that BAS-2-treated cells increased their dependence on amino acid import. To identify essential amino acids, we screened MM cells treated with BAS-2 and individually depleted each of the 20 proteinogenic amino acids. Upon depletion of either asparagine, arginine, or aspartate enhanced BAS-2 induced cell death. Combination treatment of BAS-2 and the FDA-approved drug L-asparaginase (L-ASNase), which depletes asparagine, demonstrated synergistic cytotoxicity across a panel of MM cell lines. The combination treatment induces a reliance on asparagine synthesis from pyruvate, as identified by labelling from 13C6-glucose-glucose. Mechanistically the combination induced inhibition of protein synthesis, activated the integrated stress response, and increased ATF4 and CHOP protein expression. Lastly, we showed in vivo in the chick chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model that BAS-2 and L-ASNase reduced tumour volume and CD138 positivity. In summary, these findings establish HDAC6 inhibition as a translatable metabolic target which rewires amino acid import that can be exploited with L-ASNase in MM.
